validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, actively FERC-regulated interstate gas company, independent of GEM and independent of its own website. Kinetica Energy Express, LLC (KEE) holds NGA blanket certificate Docket No. CP12-489-000, originally granted when KEE was formed in 2012 specifically to acquire Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company's ('Tennessee'/Kinder Morgan) offshore-Gulf-of-Mexico + onshore-Louisiana 'Production Area Facilities' (Federal Register 2012-08-14, Docket CP12-489-000/CP12-490-000: 'Tennessee proposes to sell to Kinetica certain pipeline systems consisting of approximately 1,300 miles of various diameter pipeline, compression facilities at three locations totaling approximately 34,250 horsepower, twelve offshore platforms, and various appurtenant and auxiliary facilities'). KEE continues filing under that same blanket certificate through at least May 2026 (Federal Register 2026-05-13: KEE requests authorization for an 11,110-hp compressor addition in Pecan Island/Acadia Parish, Louisiana, 'to alleviate system deliverability constraints...on the mainline') -- 15 distinct Federal Register notices span 2012-2026, none GEM-derived. Kinetica Partners LLC's own PHMSA-related public-safety brochure (pipelinesafetyinfo.com, one of the 3 wiki-harvested citations) independently corroborates: 'Companies operating under the Kinetica umbrella are: Transmission -- Kinetica Energy Express, LLC, Kinetica Deepwater Express, LLC; Gathering -- Kinetica Midstream Energy, LLC,' explicitly placing KEE in the Transmission category (matching GEM's PipelineType=transmission) and stating the combined Kinetica system 'span[s] the Louisiana Gulf Coast from Cameron Parish to Plaquemines Parish' -- matching GEM's own Start=Plaquemines/End=Cameron almost exactly. offshore-technology.com (GlobalData market-data page, also wiki-harvested) is a 3rd independent source confirming a 1,139km/36in gas pipeline 'operated by Kinetica Partners.' CLASSIFICATION: transmission is correct (KEE is the umbrella's transmission arm, distinct from sister entity Kinetica Midstream Energy LLC, which holds the gathering lines -- not a classification error). DUPLICATE CHECK: compared against all 49 other rows in the 50-row Gulf Coast roster; no other row names Kinetica, and none of the other Louisiana intrastate/offshore lines (Acadian, Bridgeline, LIG, RIGS, Tiger, Nautilus, Garden Banks, Mississippi Canyon, Sea Robin, Chandeleur, Destin, Independence Trail) describe the Cameron-to-Plaquemines corridor -- no duplicate found. Note for a future sweep leg (not this roster): Kinetica also operates a distinct sister transmission company, 'Kinetica Deepwater Express, LLC,' per the same PSI brochure -- if GEM tracks that entity elsewhere under a different PID, it is NOT the same physical pipe as P6005 and should not be merged. WIKI CITATION POOL: all 3 harvested citations opened and read to exhaustion (offshore-technology.com, the PSI PDF, and the 2020-05-11 Federal Register abandonment notice); none were unreadable.

validity.recommendation: do not silently accept offshore-technology.com's 'starts at Texas' framing -- it conflicts with 2 independent sources and with GEM's own (correct) Location values; treat that one line on the GlobalData profile as unreliable
validity.researcher_notes: offshore-technology.com's prose states (twice, in both the visible text and its embedded schema block) that the pipeline 'starts at Texas (the US) and ends in Louisiana (the US).' This conflicts with GEM's current StartState/Province=Louisiana (StartLocation=Plaquemines) and with 2 independent sources: (1) Kinetica Partners' own PHMSA-adjacent safety brochure, which places the entire system 'from Cameron Parish to Plaquemines Parish' -- both in Louisiana, no Texas segment; (2) every Federal Register notice I read (2012, 2020, 2021, 2026) locates KEE's physical facilities exclusively in Louisiana parishes (Vermillion, Lafourche, Acadia) and the adjoining Gulf of Mexico OCS -- 'Texas' appears in these filings only as KEE's Houston, TX mailing/headquarters address, never as a pipeline terminus. My read: the GlobalData page's 'starts at Texas' line is most likely a template artifact that conflated the company's Houston HQ address (which the same GlobalData page separately and correctly states: 'Kinetica is headquartered in Houston, Texas') with the pipeline's physical start point. GEM's own StartState/Province=Louisiana is therefore CORRECT and independently corroborated -- no change recommended -- but this GlobalData source should not be cited for the Location cell precisely because of this internal contradiction (I did not propose it as a Location ref below).

validity.recommendation: flag StartYear1=1960 as weakly sourced; a future pass should try to confirm against the original Tennessee Gas Pipeline in-service date for these facilities rather than accept the GlobalData line at face value
validity.researcher_notes: StartYear1=1960 is supported ONLY by the single offshore-technology.com/GlobalData line ('The Kinetica Energy Express project started operations in 1960'), which I could not corroborate with any second, independent source this session. Notably, Kinetica Energy Express, LLC did not exist as a certificated jurisdictional entity until 2012-2013 (FERC Docket CP12-489-000) -- '1960' is only plausible as the vintage of the underlying physical pipe when it was still part of Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company's system (TGP is one of the oldest US interstate systems and its Gulf Coast production-area facilities plausibly do predate 1960s-era construction), not as a date associated with the current corporate name. I searched for an independent second source (PHMSA NPMS/annual-report vintage data, a TGP-era FERC certificate order for the specific 'Production Area Facilities,' and Kinetica's own 'about'/history pages) but found nothing that states an in-service year for this system; kineticallc.com's about page returned 200 but contained no historical/founding-date prose I could extract. Staged at low tier rather than withheld, since GlobalData is a legitimate industry database and no source contradicts 1960 -- but this is a single-source value, flagged for further verification rather than treated as settled.

Independent of GEM; a government record naming both companies.

summary: P6005 Kinetica Energy Express: existence and transmission classification strongly confirmed (15 Federal Register notices 2012-2026 independent of GEM, plus Kinetica's own PHMSA-adjacent safety brochure), no duplicate found in the 50-row roster; Length=1139km/Diameter=36in/StartYear=1960 are each single-sourced (offshore-technology.com/GlobalData only) and staged at medium/low tier rather than high, with a flagged data-quality caveat that the same GlobalData page's 'starts at Texas' claim is contradicted by 2 independent sources and should not be used for Location. 10 of 15 worklist units filled with REFS_ADDED (Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Start, Length, Diameter, Location, Operator, Owner, plus Location's sub-fields); 5 UNRESOLVED for lack of any locatable source (Proposal, Construction, Capacity, Pressure, FuelSource, SegmentCost -- 6 actually, see file) -- none force-filled.
